blocks.text: For each property and element, the browser gathers matching declarations, compares origin, importance, layer, specificity, and order, then computes a value; some properties subsequently inherit from the parent. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Several administrative rules target one situation; an explicit stable priority decides which applies.

A selector describes target elements; keep it short and component-oriented. A long structural chain breaks when HTML changes and unnecessarily raises specificity. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

Specificity mainly compares IDs, classes/attributes, and types; source order breaks only equal priority. !important often masks confused architecture and makes states hard to override. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

color and font often inherit, while margin and border do not. DevTools Styles shows crossed-out rules and Computed reveals the final value and source. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

blocks.text: Every element generates a box made of content, padding, border, and margin. box-sizing determines whether width includes padding and border; content and context then impose minima, maxima, and overflow. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: A parcel has an item, padding, box, and surrounding clearance; stated size may include or exclude packaging.

With content-box, width covers content only; padding and border add to it. border-box makes external component dimensions more predictable. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

rem follows root size, em typography context, % the container, and viewport units the window. Use fluid sizes through min(), max(), or clamp() rather than assuming a fixed screen. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

Long text, an image without max-width, or a flex child with auto min-width can cause horizontal scrolling. Find the responsible element instead of globally hiding overflow-x. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

lessons.title: Distribute space with Flexbox and Grid
prerequisites: Know how to use a keyboard and mouse; no programming experience is assumed. The first module installs the tools and opens the project step by step.

blocks.text: Flexbox distributes space along one main axis and aligns on the cross axis; Grid defines rows and columns together. Content supplies intrinsic sizes that flex and grid negotiate with available space. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Flexbox arranges items on a shelf; Grid organizes slots in a two-dimensional cabinet.

justify-content acts on the main axis and align-items on the cross axis, whose direction depends on flex-direction. gap creates regular spacing without conditional margins. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

flex-basis proposes an initial size, grow shares surplus, and shrink absorbs shortage. min-inline-size:0 lets a child become smaller than intrinsic content. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

Grid minmax sets a useful bound and 1fr shares remaining space; auto-fit collapses empty tracks. This makes a component-driven responsive grid rather than a list of phones. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.

items.definition: Preferred size derived from content itself.

blocks.title: General application
blocks.text: Choose flex for a row/column and grid for a matrix; let content and minmax decide before adding media queries.

blocks.text: A design system names visual decisions by role rather than raw value. Components consume those tokens and define every interaction state, preserving coherence, contrast, and evolvability. Always separate the intention, the incoming data, the transformation being performed, and the observable result. This separation lets you predict behavior before running code and diagnose an error precisely.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Tokens are paint cans labeled “brand,” “danger,” and “text”; changing one recipe updates every room using it.

A semantic name like --color-danger survives a palette change unlike --red. Keep primitives limited and expose roles the team understands. Read the example from top to bottom, identify every input, and predict the output before running the command. This habit turns memorized syntax into reusable understanding.

Contrast concerns text, informative icons, essential borders, and focus. Color must never be the only signal for sale, error, or selection; add text, icon, or shape. In a real project, verify this mechanism with the browser, terminal, or DevTools instead of assuming it works. Observable evidence is more reliable than intuition.

Define default, hover, active, focus-visible, disabled, and loading. Typography keeps rem-based sizes, readable line height, and limited line length. Finally apply the concept through one small isolated change, check the result, and revert if needed. Short changes make cause and effect easy to connect.
